name: userfaultfd-open

source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for userfaultfd_behavioral.c's userfaultfd() record (flags 0x80800)

name: userfaultfd-noflags
why: userfaultfd(0) with no flags from a differently named tool is the same syscall anchor; the flag bits must not hide it
source: synthetic: an exploit PoC calling userfaultfd(0)

name: uffdio-register-ioctl
why: UFFDIO_REGISTER is an ioctl() on the uffd, the step the atomic issues right after userfaultfd(); it keeps the SYSCALL surface but is not the anchored syscall, so syscall==userfaultfd must be load-bearing
source: recorded: strace of userfaultfd_behavioral.c -- ioctl(uffd, UFFDIO_REGISTER=0xc020aa00)

name: uffdio-api-ioctl
why: UFFDIO_API is the ioctl() handshake the atomic issues immediately after userfaultfd(); it keeps the SYSCALL surface but is not userfaultfd. This replaces a prior mmap near-miss: mmap is NOT in detections/audit/atomic.rules, so it can never reach this pipeline, whereas ioctl is audited and is the real adjacent call
source: recorded: strace of userfaultfd_behavioral.c -- ioctl(uffd, UFFDIO_API=0xc018aa3f)

name: unrelated-close
why: an ordinary ioctl(fd, TCGETS) by a routine process: an audited syscall (atomic.rules records ioctl) that shares neither the anchored syscall nor its arguments -- a sanity floor that must stay quiet
source: synthetic: a routine ioctl(TCGETS), an audited high-volume syscall used as a non-firing floor
